exactIssue: Mission Control has durable supervision-feedback, reasoning-message, and owner-discovered-escape machinery, but the ordinary Chat surface had no activated rule requiring an explicit owner-marked failure to be written to that durable destination. Dedicated Mission Control-only supervisor chats and authenticated ingestion routes therefore did not imply passive capture of arbitrary ordinary Chat conversations. The result was a surface/destination activation gap: owner-reported examples could remain only in conversation context unless the active Chat separately wrote or ingested them.

relevantRule.excerpt: A later fresh owner improvement request traverses the complete capture-to-live-verification path without the owner repeating the requirement.

observedOrHypotheticalFailure: The owner expected previously identified bad-logic examples to be available as Mission Control evidence. A later Chat could not initially locate them and incorrectly investigated ChatGPT Memory instead. Repository inspection then showed that durable Mission Control capture existed, but ordinary Chat had no per-turn capture trigger tying explicit owner intent to the GitHub/runtime destination. Existing branch-local and canonical records survived; unrecorded ordinary-chat examples were recoverable only from prior-chat context where available.

evidenceRefs.meaning: Defines owner-first supervision escape assurance and reuses the append-only Mission Control ledger plus SUPERVISION_DESIGN_FEEDBACK.
Reasoning-message capture is an explicit authenticated ingestion operation with required producer/message/surface arguments; it is not ambient ordinary-chat observation.
Configured Project Manager and specialist conversations are explicitly MISSION_CONTROL_ONLY and not personal/shared-purpose chats.
supervision_design_feedback_recorded and reasoning_message_recorded are authenticated event families with bounded producer authority.
The prior owner requirement already left the next fresh owner improvement capture-to-live-verification regression unmet.

proposedChange: Add a root-bootstrap trigger for explicit owner-marked Mission Control failure capture, routed to a bounded capture pattern. When GitHub/runtime write capability is available, ordinary Chat writes the durable record itself on an isolated branch before claiming it is saved. Keep generic criticism non-publishing, preserve privacy, distinguish exact versus partial recovery, and retain existing Mission Control ledgers/templates rather than creating a new service.

alternativesConsidered.alternative: Passively ingest every ordinary ChatGPT conversation into Mission Control.
alternativesConsidered.reason: Unnecessary, privacy-invasive, and inconsistent with the dedicated MISSION_CONTROL_ONLY boundary.

alternativesConsidered.alternative: Use ChatGPT Memory as the failure store.
alternativesConsidered.reason: Memory is not the canonical Mission Control/GitHub evidence destination and cannot satisfy the existing durable-capture contract.

alternativesConsidered.alternative: Require Work/Codex to record every failure because Work implemented Mission Control.
alternativesConsidered.reason: Ordinary GitHub work belongs to Chat when available, and routing through Work adds a capability boundary without solving activation at the originating Chat surface.

risks: Without a root trigger, a future ordinary Chat can again fail to activate the Mission Control destination even though all downstream schemas exist.
Over-broad auto-capture could publish ordinary criticism or sensitive conversation content without explicit capture intent.
Recovery can create false history if paraphrases are mislabeled as exact quotes.
Branch-only evidence can be misrepresented as canonical if capture states are not explicit.
workerRecommendation: Adopt the narrow explicit-intent capture trigger, preserve capture truth states, and test it on the next fresh owner-explicit failure report before claiming universal live verification.
workerUncertainty: The GitHub implementation establishes durable capture behavior for Chat surfaces with current GitHub write access. It does not prove that every ChatGPT product surface exposes the same connector/write capability, nor does it prove a deployed Mission Control runtime ingested the GitHub artifact.
decisionThatCanChange: Whether an explicit owner request to save/recover a Mission Control failure from ordinary Chat is durably routed to Mission Control/GitHub evidence instead of being left in conversation memory.

liveVerification.trigger: Fresh owner-explicit request asking whether a newly identified humanization logic failure was saved to Mission Control lessons.
liveVerification.result: The ordinary Chat loaded the live capture rule and wrote a bounded Mission Control feedback artifact on an isolated GitHub task branch before claiming durability.
liveVerification.scope: Verifies the ordinary-Chat -> connected-GitHub capture route in the current Chat surface. Does not establish passive ingestion or universal connector availability across all ChatGPT surfaces.
